newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Creditanstalt deadline may be extended - source.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt deadline may be extended - source.

text.p: Austria may extend the bidding period for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt, even though several investors have already flagged an interest in the bank, a source close to the government said on Tuesday.
"If someone with a serious interest turns up at the last minute, we may delay the deadline by a few days," the source told Reuters.

Finance Minister Viktor Klima, who has said he wants to close the bidding period on November 15, had already received between three and five requests for a confidential information referendum on the bank, the source added.
Klima himself declined to comment on the number of bids that may already have landed on his desk. "I have a sufficient number of interested parties," he said after a cabinet meeting.
The Austrian government has been trying to offload its 70 percent voting stake in the country's flagship bank since 1991.

Another delay in selling the government's 19.9 million ordinary shares would come as little surprise to observers, who have seen a host of suitors come and go in what has become Austria's longest running privatisation since World War Two.

The latest attempt at selling the stake failed in September when a group around insurer EA-Generali bid around 6.7 billion schillings ($630.9 million) for roughly half the state's 19.9 million ordinary shares. Klima, eager to sell the share package as a whole, rejected the bid and restarted the sale.
Several international bidders were turned away over the past years by what they saw as a bias against foreigners in Austria's key political and business circles.
Klima refused to say which bidders had asked for the latest prospectus on the bank, prepared by investment house J.P Morgan which advises the government in the privatisation.

The minister, eager for billions of schillings in projected revenue to bolster his budget, wants to wrap up the sale of the bank by the end of the year. At current market prices, the government's stake is worth about 14.5 billion schillings. ($ = 10.62 Austrian Schillings)
